headline: Fragrant rice prices hit record high, increasing Tk 60-80 per kg in one month
summary: The price of various types of fragrant rice has surged by Tk 60-80 per kilogram in just one month, with traders attributing the hike to increased exports and a resulting local shortage.
details: Bangladesh's market is experiencing record-high prices for various fragrant rice varieties, with a significant increase of Tk 60 to Tk 80 per kilogram within a single month, depending on the quality.
Market observations reveal a rapid rise in the price of loose polao rice, which now sells for Tk 170-200 per kg, up from Tk 160 just a few months ago. Packaged rice prices remain at Tk 210 per kg.
Retailers and wholesalers attribute this sharp price hike primarily to increased exports of fragrant rice, which they say has created a scarcity in the local market.
Rice wholesalers further claim that heightened demand for Chinigura rice from expatriates has fueled export growth. This situation has also led to suspicions of illegal hoarding by some traders.

However, AHM Shafiquzzaman, President of CAB (Consumers Association of Bangladesh), stated that there is no actual shortage of rice in the market. He suspects that unscrupulous businesspeople are creating an artificial crisis to maximize profits.
According to data from the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB), a total of 23,959 tons of fragrant rice have been approved for export in two phases during the 2025-26 fiscal year.

headline_marked: [[Bangladesh Test openers face 4-year century drought]], struggle ahead of Australia series
headline: Bangladesh Test openers face 4-year century drought, struggle ahead of Australia series
summary: Bangladesh's opening batsmen haven't scored a century in the World Test Championship for nearly four years, raising concerns as they prepare for a challenging series against Australia.
details: Bangladesh's Test cricket team is grappling with a significant crisis in its opening batting lineup, marked by a nearly four-year drought of centuries in the World Test Championship. This long-standing issue casts a shadow over their preparations for the upcoming challenging series against Australia.

The last time a Bangladeshi opener scored a century in the World Test Championship was against India almost four years ago, by Zakir Hasan. Since then, no opener has managed to reach the three-figure mark, highlighting a severe lack of consistent performance at the top.

Following Tamim Iqbal's retirement, seven other batsmen have opened for Bangladesh in 21 matches. Collectively, they have managed only 10 half-centuries, the lowest among all teams in the Test Championship during this period, indicating a profound struggle to build solid foundations.

The current squad for the Australia tour includes Tanzid Hasan, Soumya Sarkar, and Shadman Islam. Tanzid has played only one Test, while Soumya returns to the format after five years. Shadman is considered the 'best of a bad lot' among the current options.

Injuries have further complicated team selection, with Litton Das and Shoriful Islam out of the first Test, and Nahid Rana missing the entire series. This forces selectors to rely on theoretical strengths, like Tanzid's aggressive potential and Soumya's experience on pace-friendly wickets.

Even recent century-makers like Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Shadman Islam, who scored hundreds against Ireland and Zimbabwe respectively, did so in matches outside the Test Championship. Mahmudul's form has since declined, leading to his exclusion from the Australia series squad.

Bangladesh's openers have the worst batting average in the Test Championship since early 2023, averaging just 20.17 runs per opening partnership. They remain the only team without a single century from their openers in this period.

Test captain Najmul Hossain Shanto acknowledged the challenges faced by openers, citing difficult conditions like batting at the end of a day or on wet wickets. However, he emphasized the need for them to overcome these hurdles and provide a strong start for the team.

The team is acutely aware that facing Australia's formidable pace attack, including Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, and Josh Hazlewood, will be an immense test for their struggling openers. The ability of these batsmen to withstand pace and bounce will be crucial for Bangladesh's survival in the series.
